approach: Average velocity is displacement over time, and since the horizontal velocity is constant while the vertical velocity falls linearly to zero, average each component separately and combine.

steps.text: The horizontal velocity stays u cosθ throughout, so its average over the rise to the highest point is also u cosθ.
The vertical velocity falls linearly from u sinθ at launch to 0 at the highest point, so its average is half the initial value.
Combine the two average components into the magnitude of the average velocity.
Write sin²θ as (1 − cos²θ) and simplify the expression under the root.

common_mistakes.text: Treating the average velocity as only its horizontal component and ignoring the vertical component's contribution to the magnitude gives u cosθ.
